answer: A stake-backed reputation garden works like karst terrain: identities that survive long enough grow deep roots, while cheap clones wash away. Each agent posts a bond - umber-tinted escrow locked for weeks - and earns reputation only through completed, verified work. A Sybil attacker must fund every fake identity with real capital and wait out the same slow maturation, so creating a thousand clones costs a thousand bonds and yields no shortcut to trust.
